cards.title: What the cross-wiki tier covers
cards.what_we_see: 78 language editions of the key articles ({'en': 8, 'ar': 8, 'de': 6, 'fr': 8, 'he': 6, 'nl': 8, 'pl': 7, 'pt': 8, 'ru': 7, 'es': 7, 'it': 5}), 107141 article revisions and 87429 talk revisions since 2021; 1196 term events (1192 pinned to an exact revision). One run-wide pseudonymous ID per account across all wikis.
cards.so_what: Everything below is measured on the opening sections of these pages.
cards.caveat: Term detection is a word list per language (attribution by marker words); it misses paraphrase.

cards.title: Who said it first: English led most often
cards.what_we_see: In 32 article-term cells where 2+ editions added the term after 2021, the first mover was English 9 (chance 6.35), French 6 (chance 5.48), Spanish 6 (chance 5.03), German 3 (chance 2.28), Dutch 3 (chance 5.01). English moved before the other edition in 69% of 103 pairs (chance 58%, p=0.019); 16% followed English within 90 days (chance 11%, p=0.0559). In 17 more cases English already had the term before 2021 and the other edition added it later.

null_model.null: each language's entry dates permuted across the cells where it has one (keeps each edition's general timing; breaks the link to the specific article and term)

cards.so_what: A systematic leader is the edition the others follow; a short follow lag is consistent with copying or translation.
cards.caveat: First entry only; a term can enter and leave many times. Pages created after 2021 count their creation as entry.

cards.title: From 'accused of' to fact: where the encyclopedia's own voice took over
cards.what_we_see: Article-term paths from attributed to own voice: English 12 (median 430.1 d), Hebrew 6 (median 439.7 d), Portuguese 5 (median 827.5 d), Italian 4 (median 273.2 d), Russian 4 (median 540.4 d), Dutch 3 (median 845.6 d), Arabic 3 (median 1048.5 d), Spanish 2 (median 662.3 d), French 1 (median 1242.6 d). Own-voice transitions after 7 Oct 2023 vs expected from editing activity: English 12/18 (chance 16.64, p=0.9998), German 3/3 (chance 2.87, p=0.8734), French 14/15 (chance 14.2, p=0.8119), Spanish 3/5 (chance 4.65, p=0.997), Italian 56/56 (chance 54.44, p=0.205), Dutch 7/12 (chance 11.04, p=0.9998), Russian 9/9 (chance 8.52, p=0.6118), Hebrew 5/5 (chance 4.43, p=0.5441), Arabic 3/4 (chance 3.47, p=0.9121), Polish 3/3 (chance 2.55, p=0.6119), Portuguese 10/11 (chance 10.04, p=0.7496)

null_model.null: transitions spread like the language's revisions (binomial on the after-war share of revisions)

cards.so_what: Moving a charge from someone's mouth into the encyclopedia's voice is the strongest framing change.
cards.caveat: Voice = a term sentence without an attribution word of that language (a marker heuristic, not a coded reading). English key articles from ratchet carry voice only at event revisions.

cards.title: After 7 October: which editions moved with English
cards.what_we_see: Article-term cells present on 6 Oct 2023 -> now: English 7->13, German 1->3, French 1->12, Spanish 3->10, Italian 2->6, Dutch 9->12, Russian 2->5, Hebrew 4->7, Arabic 8->15, Polish 0->4, Portuguese 6->9. Insertions after the war vs expected from editing activity: English 115 (chance 110.555), German 26 (chance 23.62), French 96 (chance 84.025), Spanish 59 (chance 56.162), Italian 75 (chance 74.205), Dutch 54 (chance 52.115), Russian 33 (chance 31.323), Hebrew 25 (chance 24.101), Arabic 22 (chance 26.801), Polish 12 (chance 10.133), Portuguese 24 (chance 23.136)

null_model.null: each page's insertion events moved to random revisions of the same page (keeps its activity curve)

cards.so_what: English gained 7 and lost 1 cells; 'net_gain_vs_english' compares each edition.
cards.caveat: Cells are article x term family; presence anywhere in the opening section.

cards.title: The same accounts across editions
cards.what_we_see: 153 of 8175 accounts (2%) edited the same key article in 2+ languages; chance 106.005 (p=0.001). Accounts that inserted a term family in 2+ languages: 0 (chance 0.0, p=1.0) of 281 inserters; removed in 2+ languages: 0 (chance 0.0, p=1.0) of 284 removers.

null_model.null: within each language, accounts shuffled among accounts with the same activity (number of articles, or families, in that language); multilingual accounts stay multilingual

cards.so_what: Above chance means multilingual editors carry the same term across editions, not just edit in several.
cards.caveat: Same username = same global (SUL) account; local accounts checked for every term-event account. 'Not detected' means our tests found nothing beyond chance; with few events the tests have little power, so it is not proof that it did not happen.

cards.title: Same-day moves in different editions
cards.what_we_see: within 1h: same account 0 pairs (chance 0.0, p=1.0), different accounts 11 (chance 5.26, p=0.031); within 1d: same account 0 pairs (chance 0.0, p=1.0), different accounts 135 (chance 104.565, p=0.014); within 1w: same account 0 pairs (chance 0.0, p=1.0), different accounts 925 (chance 579.256, p=0.001). Clusters of one term moving in 3+ editions of the same article within 48 h: 3 (chance 1.28); flagged beyond the selection-calibrated null: 0.

null_model.null: account-language timelines shifted at random (1-7 d for 1 h, 3-21 d for 1 d, 14-90 d for 1 w); clusters against the best cluster of each null world

cards.so_what: Synchrony across editions beyond chance is what coordination would look like.
cards.caveat: News also synchronises editions (an ICJ ruling, a UN report): the time-shift null removes news timing too, so a flagged cluster is a lead to read, not proof of coordination. 'Not detected' means our tests found nothing beyond chance; with few events the tests have little power, so it is not proof that it did not happen.

1h.null: each account-language timeline shifted by a random 1-7 days (either sign, wrapped)

1d.null: each account-language timeline shifted by a random 3-21 days (either sign, wrapped)

1w.null: each account-language timeline shifted by a random 14-90 days (either sign, wrapped)

campaigns.null: timelines shifted 7-60 days; each cluster's score (languages, accounts, tightness) against the best cluster of every null world

cards.title: Cross-wiki blocs
cards.what_we_see: 479 accounts with term events; 0 significant term co-activity edges (chance 0.0), 0 of them across languages; talk co-activity edges 8 (cross-language 8). Communities of 3+: 0, beyond chance: 0.

null_model.null: analyze_coord engine with degree-preserving rewiring inside each language (shared article-language units) and 1-7 d timeline shifts, whole pipeline re-run on null worlds

cards.so_what: A bloc that spans editions is the cross-wiki form of a canvassed group.
cards.caveat: Nodes are A1, A2...; units are 'article [language]'. 'Not detected' means our tests found nothing beyond chance; with few events the tests have little power, so it is not proof that it did not happen.

cards.title: Cross-wiki activity and the documented canvassing windows
cards.what_we_see: No account set large enough to test.

null_model.null: matched random account sets (same event counts), analyze_coord.window_alignment

cards.so_what: The windows are English-Wikipedia findings (ArbCom); here we ask whether cross-wiki activity clusters in them.
cards.caveat: Windows overlap the war's busiest news months; matched sets share that background. 'Not detected' means our tests found nothing beyond chance; with few events the tests have little power, so it is not proof that it did not happen.

cards.title: Court rulings said more than the courts did
cards.what_we_see: Arabic: icj_found_plausible_intent (Gaza genocide; 2024-04-17 -> 2026-10-10, still in the lead); English: icj_found_plausible_intent (Gaza genocide; 2024-03-17 -> 2024-05-05); French: icj_recognised_apartheid (Israeli apartheid; 2025-10-26 -> 2026-11-05, still in the lead); Italian: icj_plausibly_genocidal (Gaza genocide, Gaza war; 2025-03-09 -> 2026-10-28, still in the lead); Russian: court_found_israel_guilty (Israeli apartheid; 2025-03-31 -> 2026-09-24, still in the lead) What the courts said: icj_found_plausible_intent: ICJ order of 26 Jan 2024: found some of the rights South Africa claimed plausible; it made no finding of intent | icj_plausibly_genocidal: No ICJ ruling uses the phrase 'plausibly genocidal' | court_found_israel_guilty: ICJ advisory opinion of 19 Jul 2024 is non-binding and gives no verdict of guilt | icj_recognised_apartheid: ICJ advisory opinion of 19 Jul 2024 found a breach of CERD Article 3 without saying whether it was segregation or apartheid | icj_ruled_genocide: No ICJ judgment has found that Israel is committing genocide (merits pending)
cards.so_what: Turning a provisional order or a non-binding opinion into a finding is a factual error, not a framing choice.
cards.caveat: Flags are the patterns in LANGS.md finding 7 plus an English equivalent; each hit needs a human read.

cards.title: What sources came in with the term
cards.what_we_see: 622 insertions with section-0 references at both revisions; 35% brought a new domain. Arriving classes: {'Other': 1254, 'Western wire & papers': 298, 'Rights orgs & UN': 221, 'Arab & Palestinian press, pro-Palestinian outlets': 101, 'Israeli press': 92, 'Scholarly (books, journals)': 73, 'Pro-Israel advocacy': 8}. Insertions that stuck brought a new source 50% of the time vs 28% for reverted ones (difference 0.22, chance 0.001, p=0.0005).

null_model.null: stuck / reverted labels permuted across insertions

cards.so_what: Whether a framing sticks because it is sourced, or because it is pushed, is the core fairness question.
cards.caveat: Domains only (explore.SOURCE_CLASSES); citation templates without URLs count as no domain.

cards.title: Settled by a formal discussion, or by attrition?
cards.what_we_see: Of 26 English wordings that stuck (term entered or left and stayed 90+ days), 6 settled within 30 days after an RfC / move-request close (chance 2.3, p=0.0202); 9 stuck after failed attempts with no close nearby. Other editions changed the same term within 30 days after an English close 154 times (chance 192.33).

null_model.null: stick dates uniform over 2021 -> now-90 d; each page's own close dates

cards.so_what: A wording that settles right after a close was decided by the community's formal process.
cards.caveat: Close date = first signature after the close template; undated or unclosed items are counted but not aligned.
